triage_method: Every one of the 29 aghq/-prefixed required_core/compatibility_adapter rows in required-source-case-map.json was cross-referenced against its planned_case_id in aghq-required-case-plan.json's source_rows. 7 rows (the AGHQ-CTRL-* normalization control rows) point at a planned_case_id that IS one of the plan's 16 fully-specified paired_control_cases (r_call + r_assertion + julia_call + expected + acceptance_rule all present) -- those 7 are executed by this batch. The other 22 rows (AGHQ-AUTO-K-* and AGHQ-POLICY-* ) point at a *-CONTROL-CONTRACT planned_case_id that appears only in the plan's source_rows bucket, never in paired_control_cases -- no r_call/r_assertion/julia_call/expected is defined for any of them anywhere in the frozen plan, so none is executable; each is recorded verbatim under needs_new_julia_surface with its plan-frozen remaining_obligation as the reason. This batch additionally executes the 9 AGHQ-INVALID-* paired controls from the same 16-item paired_control_cases list even though those 9 rows carry classification="rejected" in required-source-case-map.json (outside the 29-row required_core/compatibility_adapter scope) -- they are still real, fully-specified executable cases in the frozen plan and dropping them would under-cover the plan's own 16-case paired-control set; each such case's source_classification_note records that it is out-of-scope for the 29-row accounting.

control_normalization_fixture.kind: pure control-normalization; no simulated data, no model fit
control_normalization_fixture.r_side_function_under_test: .gllvmTMB_normalize_aghq (R/gllvmTMB.R:2046, accessed as gllvmTMB:::.gllvmTMB_normalize_aghq since it is unexported)

negative_controls.description: compare CORE070-AGHQ-CTRL-FALSE-PAIRED-CONTROL's actual Julia result ("off") against the wrong expected label ("auto"); must NOT pass.
CORE070-AGHQ-CTRL-ONE-PAIRED-CONTROL returns 1 without throwing; asserting it against expected="ArgumentError" must NOT pass.
CORE070-AGHQ-INVALID-ZERO-PAIRED-CONTROL throws ArgumentError; asserting it against expected="off" must NOT pass.

rationale_notes: No fits are performed anywhere in this batch -- both .gllvmTMB_normalize_aghq and GLLVM._aghq_request are pure scalar-argument normalizers with no data dependency, so the whole batch runs in well under a second once the frozen R library and Julia are loaded; the >60s-Julia-precompile startup floor dominates, not the checks themselves.

R and Julia are still run as two separate processes (R computing r_assertion, the Julia child computing the native normalization independently and reading only a small boolean oracle back from R) to match the paired_control_cases' own acceptance_rule wording ('Frozen R assertion true and native normalization value/error matches') and to keep the Julia child free of any RCall dependency, per the established batch pattern.

R/aghq-control.R and R/aghq-gate.R are pinned in source_pins (matching the frozen plan's own source_pins for this annex) even though .gllvmTMB_normalize_aghq itself lives in R/gllvmTMB.R -- all four files are the frozen plan's declared provenance for the AGHQ control-normalization surface as a whole, and R/aghq-control.R plus R/aghq-gate.R gate the downstream aghq= consumption this control feeds (out of scope for THIS batch's 16 cases, but the same provenance set the plan itself pins).

The 9 AGHQ-INVALID-* cases are executed here even though required-source-case-map.json classifies their source rows 'rejected' (hence outside the 29-row required_core/compatibility_adapter scope this batch is otherwise accounting for) -- see source_classification_note on each such case.

runner.inner_invocation: julia --project=. tools/core070_aghq_batch.jl <julia-results.json> (destination path only; oracle handed via the CORE070_AGHQ_R_ORACLE env var, never RCall)
